questionSimple: Nico controls Angelina's Sir Shandlar of Eberyn enchanted with their Mark of the Oni. Angelina casts their own Steal Enchantment, targeting Nico's Mark of the Oni. After it resolves, who controls the Sir Shandlar of Eberyn? Who controls the Mark of the Oni?
answerSimple: Angelina controls both permanents. Out of the two auras, Mark of the Oni has the earlier timestamp, and would normally be applied first. However, the effects from both auras apply in the same layer, applying the Steal Enchantment's effect would change how the Mark of the Oni's effect is applied, and applying the Mark of the Oni's effect would not change how the Steal Enchantment's effect is applied, so the Mark of the Oni's effect is dependent on the Steal Enchantment's effect. The Steal Enchantment's effect applies first, giving Angelina control of Mark of the Oni, and then the Mark of the Oni's effect applies, giving Angelina control of Sir Shandlar of Eberyn.

questionSimple: Noor controls a Skeletal Snake enchanted with a Felidar Umbra. Arlo casts Annihilating Fire, targeting Skeletal Snake. What happens?
answerSimple:
Felidar Umbra is destroyed and Skeletal Snake remains on the battlefield.

There are two replacement effects trying to apply to the same event. Umbra armor is attempting to replace the destruction of the creature, while Annihilating Fire's effect is attempting to replace where the creature moves to. The "move to the graveyard" event is a part of the "destroy" event, so the umbra armor replacement effect must apply first. Once that effect has been applied, the creature is no longer about to die, so there are no more effects to apply.

If the Skeletal Snake would die later in the turn, the Annihilating Fire's replacement effect will apply at that time and cause it to move to exile instead of the graveyard.

Temple of Deceit will enter the battlefield untapped. Its enters-the-battlefield trigger will not trigger.

questionSimple: Nikolai controls a Lifeline and 2 Princess Lucrezia. Ariel casts Rout. Does Lifeline trigger and return the creatures to the battlefield at the beginning of the next end step?
answerSimple: No. Leaves-the-battlefield triggers care about the game state immediately before the event in question occurred when determining whether they trigger. There was another creature on the battlefield at that time, so Lifeline will trigger for both creatures that died. However, Lifeline has an intervening "if" clause that checks for that condition again as the trigger begins to resolve. There is not another creature on the battlefield at that time, so the ability is removed from the stack. Neither Princess Lucrezia returns to the battlefield.

questionSimple:
Which of the following cards have one or more mana abilities?

Soulbright Flamekin, Deranged Assistant, Chromatic Sphere, Keeper of Progenitus, Sarkhan, Fireblood, Sakiko, Mother of Summer, Everflowing Chalice, Inner Fire, Charmed Pendant, Forbidden Orchard, Spectral Searchlight

Triggered abilities are only mana abilities if they trigger from the activation or resolution of an activated mana ability, or from mana being added to a player's mana pool.

questionSimple: Alfonso controls Alhammarret's Archive, Thought Reflection, Blood Scrivener, Lich, and Words of Worship. Nico controls Chains of Mephistopheles, Alms Collector and Rain of Gore. Neither player has any cards in hand. Alfonso activates Words of Worship once, then moves to their draw step. What is the greatest number of cards that Alfonso can end up with in their hand, assuming they make the best possible choices? What else happens in that scenario?
answerSimple:
At most Alfonso can end up with 29 cards in their hand. Rain of Gore only applies to life gained due to a spell or ability, not a turn-based action, so it won't apply to any life gain caused by Words of Worship. Whenever multiple replacement effects apply to an event (such as Alfonso drawing a card), the affected player will chose which one to apply first. Once a replacement effect has been applied to an event, it will not apply again to that event or any events contained inside that event.

* The event begins as "draw a card". * Alfonso chooses to apply Blood Scrivener's effect. The event is "Draw 2 cards, lose 1 life". * Alfonso must apply Alms Collector's effect. The event is "Draw a card, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso chooses to apply Words of Worship's effect to their draw. The event is "Gain 5 life, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso must apply Alhammarret's Archive's first effect to the life gain. The event is "Gain 10 life, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso must apply Lich's effect to the life gain. The event is "Draw 10 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso must apply Thought Reflection's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Draw 2 cards, draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso draws a card. The event is "Draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso chooses to apply Chains of Mephistopheles's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Discard a card, draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso discards a card. The event is "Draw a card, draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso must apply Alhammarret's Archive's effect to the first card draw. The event is "Draw 2 cards, draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Alfonso draws 2 cards. The event is "Draw 9 cards, Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * For the next 9 cards draws, Alfonso chooses to apply and perform Chains of Mephistopheles's effect followed by Alhammarret's Archive and Thought Reflection's effects, making them all "discard a card, draw 4 cards". The event is "Nico draws a card, lose 1 life". * Nico must apply Chains of Mephistopheles's effect to the card draw, putting a card from their library into their graveyard. * Alfonso loses 1 life.

Alfonso has 29 cards in their hand and 10 cards in their graveyard. Nico has 1 card in their graveyard. Alfonso has lost 1 life.

questionSimple: Adeline casts Living Death while they control Immortal Coil and Walking Corpse. The only card in their graveyard is a Cheeky House-Mouse. Does Adeline lose the game? If so, could they avoid this by countering Immortal Coil's trigger with Voidslime?
answerSimple: Adeline will lose the game unless they castVoidslime. The first step in Living Death's resolution is to exile all creature cards from graveyards. questionSimple: Aspen casts Animate Dead targeting Knight of Glory in their graveyard. What happens?
answerSimple:
Both permanents end up in the graveyard.

Knight of Glory's protection ability doesn't function in the graveyard, so it's a legal target for Animate Dead. As Animate Dead's trigger resolves, first Animate Dead's enchant ability changes to "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with Animate Dead". Then Knight of Glory is returned to the battlefield. At this point the next instruction is to attach Animate Dead to Knight of Glory, but this is illegal to do because now that it's on the battlefield, Knight of Glory's protection ability is active.

After the triggered ability from Animate Dead has finished resolving, the game will check state-based actions and see that Animate Dead is an Aura that isn't enchanting anything, so it's put into its owner's graveyard.. This causes Animate Dead's leaves-the-battlefield ability to trigger, sacrificing Knight of Glory.

questionSimple: Alessandra controls Enduring Renewal and Keranos, God of Storms. During their upkeep Alessandra activates Sindbad. What happens?
answerSimple:
During the resolution of Sindbad's ability, Alessandra draws a card, and Enduring Renewal replaces this draw.

Sindbad's discard effect never happens, as the original event is replaced.

If the first revealed card is a "Creature", that card is put into the graveyard through Enduring Renewal's effect, and that card never enters Alessandra's hand. Keranos, God of Storms does not trigger, since the card is not drawn.

If the first revealed card is a "Land", Alessandra draws that card through Enduring Renewal's effect, and triggers Keranos, God of Storms. Alessandra then will attempt to draw an additional card, but must go through Enduring Renewal's replacement effect again.

If the first revealed card is neither a "Creature" nor a "Land", Alessandra draws the card and triggers Keranos, God of Storms. When they next gain priority, they put the 3 damage to any target trigger onto the stack.

questionSimple: Ashley controls Dralnu, Lich Lord, Furnace of Rath and six Swamps. Norah casts Lightning Helix targeting Dralnu, Lich Lord. If Ashley chooses to sacrifice Furnace of Rath, how many other permanents will they need to sacrifice?
answerSimple:
Two or five, Ashley's choice.

Both Dralnu, Lich Lord and Furnace of Rath have replacement effects that modify how the game handles damage that is being dealt to Dralnu, Lich Lord. As Ashley is the controller of the affected object, Ashley will choose which order to apply the replacement effects in. If Ashley chooses to apply Dralnu, Lich Lord's effect first, the 3 damage will be converted into sacrificing three permanents, and Furnace of Rath will no longer apply to that event since there's no longer any damage being dealt. If they chooses to apply Furnace of Rath first, then the three damage will be doubled to six damage, and then will be replaced by sacrificing six permanents.

Whether Ashley chooses to sacrifice Furnace of Rath or not is irrelevant, as all replacement effects are applied to the event before anything is actually sacrificed.

No. After Daydream resolves, Ashlynn receives priority.. At this point, Daydream is in the graveyard, and they can choose to cast it again. When it's cast, it goes from the graveyard to the stack. answerSimple:
Yes. The damaging ability of City of Brass is a trigger and as such goes on the stack when City of Brass is activated. However, since the activated ability of City of Brass is a mana ability, it does not go on the stack and instead is resolved instantly. This means that when Abdiel activates the mana ability of City of Brass, they will get one mana, then the triggered ability goes on the stack. With their newfound mana, they can cast Angel's Grace in response to the trigger. 

If instead Abdiel decided to first cast Angel's Grace and activates City of Brass during the casting process, they would lose the game as the triggered ability would go on the stack above Angel's Grace and resolve first.

questionSimple: Alice controls Battle Hurda and Devoted Hero. Alice attacks with both creatures, and after Battle Hurda has dealt its damage Nicolas casts Lightning Blow targeting Devoted Hero. Will Devoted Hero deal damage this turn?
answerSimple: Yes. As the combat damage step begins, the game checks to see if there are any creatures in combat that have either first strike or double strike. If there are, it generates an additional combat damage step. In the first one, only creatures with first strike or double strike will deal damage. In the second combat damage step, the creatures that deal damage are the ones that didn't have either first strike or double strike as the first combat damage step began. Devoted Hero gained first strike after the first combat damage step began, and therefore will still deal damage in the second one.

questionSimple: Noemi controls Memnite and Cyclops of One-Eyed Pass. Adrian casts Massacre Girl. In response to Massacre Girl's trigger Noemi casts Nasty End, choosing to sacrifice Memnite. After everything has resolved, what does the battlefield look like?
answerSimple:
Cyclops of One-Eyed Pass and Massacre Girl are still alive. When Massacre Girl's trigger resolves, Cyclops of One-Eyed Pass will get -1/-1 and won't die.

Massacre Girl's triggered ability consists of two parts: a trigger that gives all creatures -1/-1 when it enters, and a text that sets up a delayed trigger that will cause a -1/-1 trigger to be put onto the stack every time something dies. At the time Memnite dies, Massacre Girl's triggered ability hasn't resolved yet, and hasn't set up the delayed trigger, therefore nothing new will be added to the stack.

questionSimple: Azariah controls Night of Souls' Betrayal and casts Watcher for Tomorrow. What happens as Watcher for Tomorrow resolves?
answerSimple:
When Watcher for Tomorrow enters the battlefield tapped, its hideaway ability triggers, but isn't placed on the stack until Azariah would get priority. Before Azariah gets priority state-based actions are checked and Watcher for Tomorrow is put into the graveyard for having 0 or less toughness. Then, its "leaves" trigger triggers but is not placed onto the stack. Since no more state based actions are completed, Azariah gets priority and has two triggers to place onto the stack in an order of their choice.

If Azariah chooses to have Watcher for Tomorrow's hideaway trigger resolve first they will exile a card face down then put it into their hand. If the triggers resolve in the other order, Watcher for Tomorrow's "leave" trigger will resolve returning nothing, then Azariah will exile a card face down with no way to return it to hand.

questionSimple: Armani attacks with Rockslide Elemental, which has 4 +1/+1 counters. Nico blocks with Tephraderm. What happens to Rockslide Elemental in the first combat damage step?
answerSimple:
Tephraderm will trigger upon combat damage being dealt, and Rockslide Elemental will trigger as Tephraderm dies after SBAs are checked. Since there are now multiple triggers waiting to be placed on the stack, Armani and Nico will do so respectively in APNAP order.

Yes.

questionSimple: Allyson controls Whiptail Wurm which is enchanted by Witness Protection. Whiptail Wurm then becomes enchanted by One with the Stars. What happens?
answerSimple:
Whiptail Wurm becomes an enchantment with no abilities and with the color dictated by Witness Protection. When state-based actions are checked, Witness Protection is attached to an illegal target and is put into the graveyard. Whiptail Wurm then regains all characteristics except its type is only enchantment. State-based actions are checked again. Nothing happens, and Allyson gets priority.

This is an interaction of continuous effects, so the layers will need to be considered. In this case, no changes occur until layer four. There are two effects occurring in this layer, so timestamps will need to be considered. Since Witness Protection was attached first, Whiptail Wurm maintains its status as a creature. Then, One with the Stars turns Whiptail Wurm into an enchantment and removes all other types. Whiptail Wurm is changed to the color dictated by Witness Protection in layer five. Whiptail Wurm loses all abilities in layer six due to Witness Protection. Lastly, Whiptail Wurm has its power and toughness set to the values stated in Witness Protection in layer seven. When state-based actions are checked, Witness Protection is attached to an enchantment and is put into the graveyard. State-based actions are checked again, and nothing happens.

questionSimple: Axel control Viscera Seer, Hateful Eidolon, and Pillarfield Ox enchanted by Blessing of the Nephilim. Axel activated Viscera Seer's ability sacrificing Pillarfield Ox to do so. This triggers Hateful Eidolon. In what order can Axel resolve these abilities?

Axel must draw then scry 1.

Seven. Zilortha, Strength Incarnate's ability means that for damage assignment purposes Phyrexian Walker is treated as if it has zero toughness. It therefore already has lethal damage marked on it, and Carnage Tyrant can trample over it for the full 7.

questionSimple: Aden controls Krark, the Thumbless and casts Vibrant Outburst targeting Naomi. In response to Krark, the Thumbless' trigger, Naomi casts Put Away, countering Vibrant Outburst. What happens when Krark, the Thumbless' trigger resolves?
answerSimple:
Aden flips a coin. If they win, they copy Vibrant Outburst and may choose new targets for it. If they lose, nothing happens.

When resolving Krark, the Thumbless' ability, if Aden wins the flip, the ability requires information about Vibrant Outburst in order to copy it, but it is no longer on the stack. In this case, the last known information about the spell is used, and the copy is created. However, if Aden loses the flip, Krark, the Thumbless' ability can no longer find the spell on the stack to return it to hand, since it is now a new object in Aden's graveyard.. In this case, since no information about the spell is required to perform the effect, the effect simply does nothing.

questionSimple: Agustin has unlimited blue mana and casts Ghostly Flicker targeting Court Hussar and Mystic Sanctuary. They put Court Hussar's trigger on the stack first, then Mystic Sanctuary's afterwards. They have Mystic Sanctuary put Ghostly Flicker on top of their library and upon the resolution of Court Hussar's ability they'll select Ghostly Flicker out of the top three cards and put the other two on the bottom. Since they can repeat this any number of times, will they be able to sort their deck into any order?
answerSimple: It depends. This loop can eventually sort the deck if it contains an odd number of cards after Court Hussar's trigger resolves. If the deck is even, the general deck order must be preserved and cannot be sorted. The deck can be "cut" into two even stacks to any 2-card pair and that card pair can be set in any order. The order or every other 2-card pair can also be relatively set by Agustin.
answerSimpleCited: It depends. This loop can eventually sort the deck if it contains an odd number of cards after Court Hussar's trigger resolves. If the deck is even, the general deck order must be preserved and cannot be sorted. The deck can be "cut" into two even stacks to any 2-card pair and that card pair can be set in any order. Master Biomancer's effect needs to be applied first since none of the other effects apply to Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider entering without counters. questionSimple: Alex controls Bag of Holding and activates its first activated ability. When it resolves they draw a card and discard Archfiend of Spite. What happens?
answerSimple:
Alex can cast Archfiend of Spite. If they don't, it will either end up in exile or the graveyard, depending on the order in which they put the triggers on the stack.

When Archfiend of Spite is discarded, it's exiled instead of going to the graveyard. Alex can then choose in what order to put the triggers onto the stack. If the madness trigger resolves first and Alex doesn't cast it, it's put into their graveyard and then exiled to Bag of Holding. Then when the madness trigger resolves, if Alex doesn't cast it, it'll be moved to their graveyard.

questionSimple: In a Commander game with 4 players, Ashley casts Kardur, Doomscourge. Brayan controls Frost Ogre, and Parhelion II, which is not a creature at the time Kardur, Doomscourge's enter the battlefield ability resolves. During Brayan's next turn, can they attack Ashley with Parhelion II? Can they have the Angel tokens created by Parhelion II attack Ashley?
answerSimple:
Brayan cannot attack Ashley with Parhelion II, but they can choose for the Angel tokens to attack Ashley.

Kardur, Doomscourge's enters-the-battlefield ability sets up a rules change that causes any creatures Ashley's opponents control to have to attack if able and to have to attack another player if able. Since this is a change in the rules of the game, it affects Parhelion II even if it is not a creature at the time the ability resolves.

The Angel tokens are created attacking, but are never declared as attackers. Because of this, Brayan can choose Ashley to be the defending player for the tokens.

Harness the Storm doesn't create an alternative cost the way As Foretold does, it actually requires the player to pay the spell's mana cost. This ability triggers while Armando is casting the spell, and is put on the stack above the spell as soon as they are done casting it and before they would get priority again. It uses the last-known information of the spell on the stack in order to make the copy.

questionSimple: Annabelle and Nico each control a copy of Gisela, Blade of Goldnight. If Annabelle attacks with Venser's Sliver and it isn't blocked, how much damage would it deal to Nico?
answerSimple:
Venser's Sliver would deal 2 or 3 damage, Nico's choice. Gisela, Blade of Goldnight has a static ability that sets up a prevention effect for damage being dealt. Since both copies of Gisela, Blade of Goldnight are trying to replace the damage dealt to Nico, they get to choose in which order they are applied. 

If Nico chooses to apply their own Gisela, Blade of Goldnight's replacement effect first, the 3 damage would be halved and rounded down to 1. Then Annabelle's Gisela, Blade of Goldnight doubles the damage up to 2.

If instead Nico chose to apply Annabelle's Gisela, Blade of Goldnight's replacement effect to the damage event first, the 3 damage would first be doubled to 6. Then Nico's own Gisela, Blade of Goldnight would halve the damage down to 3.

questionSimple: Anabelle controls Muraganda Petroglyphs and Wayward Angel, and has more than 7 cards in their graveyard. Nico casts and resolves Humility. What are Wayward Angel's characteristics?
answerSimple:
Wayward Angel is a Black, 6/6 creature with no abilities. The rest of its characteristics remain the same as printed on the card. 
Wayward Angel's threshold ability changes both its color, abilities, and P/T. Therefore, it applies in layers 5, 6, and 7 with the appropriate parts applying in their appropriate layers, and the layers are applied in order. Similarly, Humility's effect is applied in layers 6 and 7, as appropriate. 
Applying layers in order:
- In layer 5, Wayward Angel becomes black. 
- In layer 6 there are two contending effects: Wayward Angel's ability giving it trample and an upkeep triggered ability, and Humility's ability removing all abilities from Wayward Angel. There is no dependency between the two, since Wayward Angel's ability has already started applying in a previous layer, and will continue to apply even if removed by Humility's ability. The effects are then applied in timestamp order with Wayward Angel's ability applying first, since it has an earlier timestamp. So in layer 6, Wayward Angel first gains trample and "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a creature.", and then loses all abilities to Humility.
- In layer 7, P/T setting effects are applied first, so that Humility first turns Wayward Angel into a 1/1. Then effects modifying P/T are applied, of which there are two: Wayward Angel's own ability that, even though removed, continues to apply and gives it +3/+3, and Muraganda Petroglyphs's ability giving Wayward Angel +2/+2 since it now has no abilities. Wayward Angel's P/T is finally 6/6.

questionSimple: Ari controls a Mirage Mirror that last turn become a copy of Angel of Condemnation and exiled Orazca Raptor with its second activated ability. This turn, Ari activates Mirage Mirror targeting Undiscovered Paradise and taps it for mana. On Ari's next turn, will the Orazca Raptor return to the battlefield? If so, can it attack?
answerSimple:
This can't happen as described. Mirage Mirror was exerted last turn, so it won't untap this turn and cannot be tapped for mana.

If it had instead been exerted two turns ago, the Orazca Raptor would return to the battlefield, but can't attack. Any time an object refers to itself by name, it just means "this card", so Mirage Mirror will return to Ari's hand during their untap step, and the Orazca Raptor will return to the battlefield. During the combat phase of that turn, Orazca Raptor has not been on the battlefield since the turn began, so it will not be able to attack.
answerSimpleCited:

questionSimple: Nico controls a Lifeline and 2 Durkwood Boars. Aniya casts Mogg Infestation. Does Lifeline trigger and return the creatures to the battlefield at the beginning of the next end step?
answerSimple: Yes. Leaves-the-battlefield triggers care about the game state immediately before the event in question occurred when determining whether they trigger. There was another creature on the battlefield at that time, so Lifeline will trigger for both creatures that died. Lifeline's trigger has an intervening "if" clause that checks for that condition again as the trigger begins to resolve. There is another creature on the battlefield at that time, created by the Mogg Infestation, so the ability resolves and will return both Durkwood Boars to the battlefield.

questionSimple: Anton attacks with Nessian Boar and Silkenfist Fighter, which Nico blocks with Imperial Outrider and Lagac Lizard, respectively. Anton then activates Sorrow's Path targeting Imperial Outrider and Lagac Lizard. Do Nessian Boar and Silkenfist Fighter trigger again?
answerSimple:
Nessian Boar triggers again, Silkenfist Fighter does not.

Nessian Boar's trigger is looking to see when a creature starts blocking Nessian Boar. Sorrow's Path causes Lagac Lizard to start blocking Nessian Boar, so it triggers again.

Silkenfist Fighter's trigger is looking to see when Silkenfist Fighter changes from being an unblocked creature to being a blocked creature. Sorrow's Path doesn't cause Silkenfist Fighter to become unblocked, it just removes its blockers and then assigns it a new one. It remains a blocked creature throughout the resolution of the ability, so it does not trigger again.
answerSimpleCited:
Nessian Boar triggers again, Silkenfist Fighter does not.

Silkenfist Fighter's trigger is looking to see when Silkenfist Fighter changes from being an unblocked creature to being a blocked creature. (509.3c) Sorrow's Path doesn't cause Silkenfist Fighter to become unblocked, it just removes its blockers and then assigns it a new one. questionSimple: Avery controls Sylvan Library and has three Life from the Loams in their graveyard. In their draw step, can they choose to dredge all three? If so, do they have to put any back on top of the library and/or pay any life?
answerSimple:
Avery can dredge all three, and won't have to put any back or pay any life.

The instructions on Sylvan Library are followed in order. Avery first chooses whether they want to draw two cards, and they're allowed to choose the affirmative even if they're planning to replace the card draws with dredge.

After dredging, Avery is instructed to choose two cards in their hand that were drawn this turn. There are no cards in Avery's hand that were drawn this turn, so Avery can't do that. The "for each" clause then does nothing, because it's referring to 0 cards. (Just like how Killing Wave doesn't make a player pay life if they don't control any creatures.)

Neither creature dies, and Ashley gains 1 life.

Grindstone's ability will still resolve and mill Nathaniel's library. questionSimple:
Alena controls a Founding the Third Path, and its third ability is resolving. Alena chooses to cast a Fatal Push from their graveyard. Alena currently does not have Revolt.
Can Alena choose to target Blockade Runner with Fatal Push? Will Blockade Runner be destroyed by Fatal Push?
answerSimple:
Yes Alena can target Blockade Runner, and it will be destroyed by Fatal Push.

Fatal Push does not check for the target's mana value when put on the stack, so Alena is allowed to target Blockade Runner.

Alena will put Fatal Push on the stack as part of the resolution of Founding the Third Path's third chapter. Once the ability is done resolving, SBAs are checked and the saga is sacrificed. In particular this means that Alena will have Revolt when Fatal Push resolves, thus Blockade Runner will get destroyed.
